newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end steady, shake off political woes.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end steady, shake off political woes.

text.p: Italian shares finished largely steady on Tuesday as many investors shook off concerns over domestic political worries facing Italy's centre-left government this week and the lower early trend on Wall Street.

Italy's government faces a vote in the lower chamber of Parliament Wednesday over sending an Italian-led multinational force to Albania with the Communist Refoundation threatening to vote against government. Dealers say even if government survives it could put a questionmark over its future credibility.
Blue-chip Mib30 index ended up 0.01 percent at 17,631 while all-share Mibtel closed 0.1 percent lower at 11,920.

Dealers said domestic investors were largely unruffled by the government's latest woes and saw some compromise being hammered out, but some international players were avoiding Italy until the political picture becomes clearer.

The government is expected to win an Albania vote in the upper house Senate later today, but it relies on Communist support in the lower house of parliament and may struggle on Wednesday to survive this vote.
However, many saw some deal being reached to help the government survive and the lira was unruffled and held steady against the German mark at around 986 lire per mark.
Among the blue chip stocks, shares in industrial group Fiat perked up to show a gain of 1.29 percent to 5,404 lire, while Montedison ended up 0.73 percent at 1,098 lire.

Olivetti closed off 1.44 percent at 603.1 lire on concern that U.S. partner Bell Atlantic is not fully happy with a recent Infostrada-France Telecom deal, while Olivetti-led Omnitel said it added 200,000 new mobile phone users in the first quarter.
San Paolo was up 0.53 percent to 11,040 lire and investment bank IMI off 0.02 percent at 15,024 lire, after IMI confirmed it was willing to become a core shareholder in Italy's largest banking group.
